1350 E 750 N, Orem, UT 84097 (former girls campus; now Provo Canyon Behavioral Hospital)

pastOperators: Robert H. Crist and Jack Williams (founders; Dennis Eugene Thorne co-owner 1978-1986)

notes: Operations suspended: the Utah Department of Health and Human Services revoked the Provo campus license (93696) on July 17, 2026 and ordered the campus to cease operations by August 16, 2026; the Springville campus license (93697) was revoked as well. The school appealed both orders on July 27, 2026 and the appeal is pending.
Shut down in 1974 over child abuse and neglect allegations; reopened the same year.

Provo campus placed on conditional status in 2012 after a runaway caused a fatal crash; Springville campus placed on conditional status in 2013 after a restraint injury; both licenses were conditional at revocation.

customIncidents: 1974: shut down over child abuse and neglect allegations; reopened the same year
1980: federal jury sides with the school in Milonas and Rice; judge issues permanent injunction against polygraphs, mail censorship, and isolation or force except for immediate danger
2004: parent complaint alleges a 15-year-old's nose was broken before a forced Haldol injection and children were held in Observation most of the day
2012: Provo campus placed on conditional status after a runaway stole a car and caused a fatal crash
2013: Springville campus placed on conditional status after a girl was injured in a restraint
2015-2020: 341 Office of Licensing investigations, 27 substantiated violations
September 2024: staff member arrested for striking a 15-year-old during a restraint; guilty plea July 2025
December 1, 2024: staff member struck a client during a restraint (substantiated, repeat noncompliance)
April 13, 2025: staff member injured a client's face during a restraint (substantiated)
June 2026: licensers sanction the school for delaying care to a teen with a jaw injury and brain bleed; two families sue
July 17, 2026: Provo campus license revoked; Springville license revoked; operations ordered to cease; appeal filed July 27

notes: Founded 1971 as an all-boys program by Robert H. Crist and Jack Williams; the girls program opened in Orem and moved to a new Springville campus in 2005. Elementary and transition programs have operated in Orem.
Considered a hub of the troubled teen industry: WWASP's founders and much of its staff came from PCS.
Tuition reported at more than $12,500 per month; average stay 8 to 12 months, often longer.
Utah Office of Licensing records mirrored on this site: Springville campus 64 inspections and 7 substantiated findings, December 2022 to August 2025; Provo campus 18 inspections in the same period.
Profile assembled by Kids Over Profits on 2026-09-11 from site records; see the Facility Profile post for sources.
